title: Pointwise colimits for a topology generated by finite one-hypercovers
statement: Let C be a category and J a Grothendieck topology generated by its finite one-hypercovers. Let A be a coefficient category, and I a diagram category. Assume I-shaped colimits exist in A and the functor colim:(I→A)→A preserves finite limits. Then the inclusion Sh(J,A)→PSh(C,A) preserves I-shaped colimits. No concreteness assumption on A is needed. The assertion includes the empty diagram.

source.place: Lemma lemma-directed-colimits-sections, Tag 0738, finite sheaf-condition argument; generalized here from filtered set-colimits to any coefficient colimit preserving finite limits.

proof.text: Package a diagram of sheaves into a presheaf with values in the diagram category I→A. Each evaluation is a sheaf. Joint reflection of limits by evaluations proves the packaged presheaf satisfies every sheaf multifork.

A finite one-hypercover has a finite multicospan index category. Applying the coefficient colimit functor preserves its limiting multifork. The explicit comparison is the identity on each object and arrow, so the resulting multifork is the sheaf multifork of the pointwise colimit.

The pointwise colimit is consequently a sheaf, because finite one-hypercovers generate J. Mathlib Sheaf.createsColimitOfIsSheaf creates the sheaf colimit from it. Thus inclusion preserves the colimit.
